text:
Maria: heads-up — after the eu-west-1 scale-up this morning, a few services started getting 5xx when fetching model artifacts from our private model-bucket endpoint. Seems intermittent, started ~08:12 UTC.
Alex: can you paste a sample error? 5xx from gateway or connection refused?
Maria: stack traces show TLS handshake timeouts and occasionally connections to public IPs. Example from pod: `GET https://models.internal-redwood.s3.amazonaws.com/abc.tar` -> connection timeout, then fallback to public and 403.
Priya: that smells like DNS split-horizon or the VPC hosted zone not being used. Any chance the route53 assoc was removed during the account migration last week?
Maria: I checked: the interface endpoint exists, ENIs are up in subnets a/b, SG attached. But `dig models.internal-redwood.s3.amazonaws.com +short` from a node returns the public S3 IPs, not the VPC endpoint ENI IPs.
Nate: interesting — can you show `ip route` and `nslookup` from the pod?
Maria: from an affected node: ```
$ dig models.internal-redwood.s3.amazonaws.com +short
52.216.12.34
52.216.12.56
```
and `ip route` shows default via nat-gw in private subnet. No special route for the endpoint.
Alex: interface endpoints rely on private hosted zone association so that DNS resolves to the ENI IPs. If dig returns public IPs, the hosted zone association may be missing or Route53 resolver rules are overriding.
Priya: did terraform run for the VPC endpoints after the migration? I remember a change to the account's cross-account associations — terraform might not re-associate hosted zones across accounts without explicit provider alias.
Maria: terraform plan shows the endpoint resource unchanged, but `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc` shows `PrivateDnsEnabled: true` but `DnsEntries` is empty.
Nate: that’s the crux. Private DNS should list the hosted zone names and ENI IPs. If it's empty the resolver doesn't rewrite. Could be an IAM permission/role issue when the endpoint was recreated in the target account.
infra-oncall: I'm checking cloudtrail for the endpoint create/update events. There's a `ModifyVpcEndpoint` at 07:59 UTC with principal arn:aws:iam::999999999:role/infra-automation — that role lost permission to associate hosted zone when we rolled the cross-account policy last month.
Priya: confirmed — the automation lacked `route53:AssociateHostedZone` across accounts. The endpoint creation succeeded but the private hosted zone association failed silently.
Maria: ok makes sense. Quick question — while we fix iam/policy, any mitigation so pods stop failing? We have model fetches on startup that break new replicas.
Alex: two short-term options: 1) Add an explicit /etc/hosts entry in the node bootstrap for models.internal-redwood.s3.amazonaws.com -> ENI IPs (ugly, transient), or 2) route traffic for S3 to the interface endpoint by IP using iptables DNAT to the ENI IP (also ugly). Better: attach a resolver rule in the VPC to force forwarding of `s3.amazonaws.com` to the Route53 inbound resolver in the endpoint account if available.
Nate: also you can pin model downloads to use the endpoint-specific host header `vpce-abcdef.s3-vpce-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` — that resolves to the endpoint by name. Might be easiest for the service patch.
Maria: can we update the service to prefer vpce hostnames as a patch? Rolling patch will take ~20m.
Priya: I'll fix the infra automation perms now (adding route53:AssociateHostedZone and route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets across the accounts) and force a `ModifyVpcEndpoint` to re-trigger the association. After that please test and report back.
deploy-bot: redeploy job queued: service/model-loader patch-vpce-hostname -> 6 pods rolling, ETA 22m.
Maria: patch rolling now. Also tagging this as incident with low sev. Will validate after infra fix.
infra-oncall: infra perms updated and `ModifyVpcEndpoint` invoked at 08:45 UTC. Route53 associations show the private hosted zone linked to vpce-0abc now.
Maria: re-tested `dig` from node: ```
$ dig models.internal-redwood.s3.amazonaws.com +short
10.0.45.12
10.0.45.13
```
Maria: pods that rolled after the patch now fetch artifacts normally. Old pods still had cached DNS entries and failed until TTL expired (~60s).
Priya: root cause summary: endpoint created/recreated during cross-account migration but automation lacked cross-account route53 permissions so private hosted zone association didn't happen. DNS fell back to public S3 IPs -> traffic to IGW/NAT -> 403/timeout because bucket policy denies public access. Fix: add route53 assoc permission, re-modify endpoint, and update automation to validate dns entries post-create.
Alex: can we add a post-create check in the automation that does `dig` and verifies ENI IPs are returned, and fail loudly if not?
Priya: yes will add that and a terraform plan-time check.
Maria: thanks all — closing once post-mortem note is in the incident tracker. :thumbsup:
